text:
The response breaks the explicit limit. It runs to roughly 190 words against a cap of 120, and it wastes words on filler such as "I would like to let you know", "Turning to concessions", "Finally, I want to reassure you" and "For your information".

There is also an accuracy problem. It says the $9 daily concession "will be replaced" by the weekly pass. The article says only that concession parking is extended and that the weekly pass can be applied for, and it does not say the daily rate is abolished. The "$15 weekly" figure, the dates, the fee increases, the 180 closed spaces, the 18-month repair time and the 2,000-signature petition are all correct. The line that the "additional revenue will be used to fund repairs" is a fair paraphrase.

It covers most key points. It leaves out the practical upside for frequent visitors, which is that the weekly pass can cost less than they pay now. It also omits that the repairs will reopen the closed levels in stages. Including the petition and the staff point is reasonable, but a manager would have been better served by trimming the repair and application detail.

The word-limit failure, the unsupported "replaced" claim and the padding make this a weak response, though most of the facts are right.

Score: 3
